facts.claim: "One More Shot" was released on October 5, 2022 as a single. It is credited to Cillables, LLC under exclusive license to Warner Records, in association with Interlude Records.
The song was written by Cil (Cecilia Webber), Annika Wells and Dan Gleyzer.
Dan Gleyzer produced the song and is credited with programming and all instruments. Cil is credited with vocals.
Yianni Anastos-Prastacos mixed the song and Dale Becker mastered it.
The lyrics tell a revenge story. The narrator catches a lover cheating and doing drugs, and she offers him "one more shot" in a darkly violent way.

Music press described it as Cil's debut single and said it was gaining traction on TikTok. It was also described as a love song that avoids cliché, builds tension over about two minutes, and showcases her vocal range.
A "One Take Version" was released on March 3, 2023. The song also appears on her EP Tears Dry On Their Own, released June 2, 2023.

In an interview, Cil said "One More Shot" was the only song she had out when she played her first show. She also named it, with "Bloodsucker" and "pretty years", as a song she can count on performing at every show.
Cil (pronounced SIL) was born in Colorado and is based in Los Angeles. By early 2025 the song had passed 60 million streams, and her follow-up "Bloodsucker" had drawn praise from Billboard.
Cil moved to Los Angeles alone in April 2021 at age 18 to pursue music. She cites Stevie Nicks, Etta James, Aretha Franklin, Amy Winehouse, Adele and Lana Del Rey as influences.

research.lineage: Cil's sound is described as a mix of pop and soul, a soulful pop style in the line of Amy Winehouse, Etta James and Lana Del Rey.

draft:
The cruelest image in **One More Shot** is a wedding dress. "You dressed me in white / To just lay me down," Cil sings, and the line folds a bride and a body into one picture. The white was supposed to mean forever, and it became a shroud. The rest of the song grows out of that image. She says she would have stayed until death took her, in the language of a vow, and then he handed her the gun himself.

The title carries two meanings. One more shot is a second chance and a bullet, and the song never chooses between them. Cil wrote it with Annika Wells and Dan Gleyzer, and they keep both meanings tangled through every chorus. She offers forgiveness in the same breath that she describes his body going cold. The song opens on a claim of victory and a gloat that he must regret things now. But the second verse shows how long the hurt has been building. She used to hold him through the night, until she noticed the purple under his eyes, the drugs he pretends are behind him, the bruise on his neck she didn't put there. "Oh, I'm not surprised," she sings. It's the saddest line in the song, because being surprised would mean she still expected better.

Then the bridge breaks the act. Whether she kills him depends on whether he's sorry. The revenge fantasy turns out to be a plea, and the menace is how a person who's been lied to keeps from begging. Listen to the chorus shift between rounds. The first time, she accuses him of wanting to leave. The second time, she tells him to go if he wants to. The rage hasn't cooled, but that permission is the closest she comes to letting him go.

Gleyzer produced the track, programmed it and played every instrument, and he keeps it lean. A steady, driving beat with a hard snare sits under a bass line that barely moves, with piano chords on top and a synth pad filling in underneath. Yianni Anastos-Prastacos mixed it dry and close, so nothing stands between you and the voice. Cil's tone is mid-range with a slight rasp, and that grain makes the threats sound like confessions. It's soul-pop in the line of the singers she names as influences, Amy Winehouse, Etta James and Lana Del Rey. It takes the wronged-woman tradition of torch songs and plays it over a spare, programmed pop frame.

This was her debut single, released about a year and a half after she moved to Los Angeles alone at 18. It caught on through TikTok and passed 60 million streams. It was the only song she had out when she played her first show, and she still counts on performing it at every one.

It sticks because it lets you say the vicious thing out loud and still hear, underneath, how badly she wanted him to stay.

factCheck.claim: Lyric quote: "You dressed me in white / To just lay me down"
factCheck.note: Matches the lyrics exactly. Two consecutive lines.

factCheck.claim: The image is a wedding dress / bride and body / shroud
factCheck.note: The lyric says only "dressed me in white." Reworded as a white dress, with the bride reading kept as interpretation.

factCheck.claim: She would have stayed until death took her, and then he handed her the gun
factCheck.note: Matches "I would've stayed 'til death took me out" and "you fucked up and gave me the gun."

factCheck.claim: Cil wrote it with Annika Wells and Dan Gleyzer
factCheck.note: Songwriting credits.
